# Philippa Gordon

## Overview

- **Age:** Early twenties  <sub>[v3 c4 P46](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0046), [v3 c26 P1](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0001)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c4 P32](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0032)</sub>
- **Status:** Engaged to Jonas Blake  <sub>[v3 c27 P17](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0017), [v3 c27 P31](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0031)</sub>
- **Origin:** Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia  <sub>[v3 c4 P32](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0032), [v3 c4 P33](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0033)</sub>
- **Role:** Redmond College student  <sub>[v3 c4 P46](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0046), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Phil  <sub>[v3 c4 P28](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0028)</sub>

## Appearance

Philippa is a remarkably beautiful girl with big, velvety brown eyes, rose-red lips, a soft, ripe glow on her cheeks, and a delightfully crooked, bewitching smile over very white little teeth. She has satin-smooth, brown-tinted hair and dark, oddly-pointed eyebrows. Though a bit concerned about her nose developing family tendencies, she is widely celebrated as the handsomest girl and belle at Redmond College.

_Sources: [v3 c4 P20](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0020), [v3 c4 P36](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0036), [v3 c4 P41](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0041), [v3 c4 P56](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0056), [v3 c26 P1](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0001), [v3 c35 P6](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0006)_

## Personality

Philippa is a gay, carefree, and irrepressibly lively young woman who loves fun and social merriment. She is hopelessly indecisive about life's practical choices, often leaving her options open or relying on chance and others to make up her mind for her. Underneath her frivolous, lighthearted exterior lies an intensely loyal, sweet, and humble friend who is free from snobbery or envy. She has a keen intellect when she chooses to use it, easily excelling in her studies despite her whimsical nature.

_Sources: [v3 c4 P28](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0028), [v3 c4 P46](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0046), [v3 c4 P48](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0048), [v3 c4 P61](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0061), [v3 c5 P2](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0002), [v3 c20 P7](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0007), [v3 c27 P19](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0019)_

## History

Philippa Gordon arrived at Redmond College in Kingsport, initially feeling lonesome until she encountered Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in Old St. John's Cemetery. She quickly struck up an affectionate friendship with them and brought them into her wide social circle. During her first year, she struggled to choose between her two home suitors, Alec and Alonzo, while enjoying the devotion of numerous campus admirers. Prior to their second year at Redmond, she joined Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard in renting Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, where they lived with Aunt Jamesina. Over a summer at Prospect Point, she met Jonas Blake, an earnest and homely theology student; despite her previous declarations that she must marry a rich and handsome man, she fell deeply in love with him. After finally declining her former suitors, she happily accepted Jonas's proposal during her Junior year. Upon completing her Arts course at Redmond, Philippa married Jonas in a June wedding and moved to his mission parish in the Patterson Street slums.

_Sources: [v3 c4 P20](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0020), [v3 c4 P24](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0024), [v3 c4 P50](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0050), [v3 c5 P2](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0002), [v3 c10 P48](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0048), [v3 c24 P8](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0008), [v3 c24 P21](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0021), [v3 c27 P17](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0017), [v3 c27 P29](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0029), [v3 c39 P39](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0039)_

## Quotes

> My mission is, as Josiah Allen says, 'to charm and allure.'  <sub>[v3 c20 P7](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0007)</sub>

> Better a dinner of herbs where your chums are than a stalled ox in a lonely boardinghouse.  <sub>[v3 c10 P53](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0053)</sub>

> I can make up my own mind for once and it was real easy, too. It's very delightful to feel so sure, and know it's your own sureness and not somebody else's.  <sub>[v3 c27 P23](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0023)</sub>

> I shall be poor as gaily as I've been rich. You'll see. I'm going to learn how to cook and make over dresses.  <sub>[v3 c27 P31](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0031)</sub>

> I was born a see-saw, Aunty, and nothing can ever prevent me from teetering.  <sub>[v3 c19 P22](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0022)</sub>
